subject: science
question_text: What are the different means by which infectious diseases are spread?
answer_text: Infectious diseases spread by different means. These are: a) Through air: An infected person when sneezes or coughs releases droplets containing germs which infect another healthy person through air and microbes enter a new body. Examples: common cold, pneumonia and tuberculosis. b) Through water: contaminated water will infect many people and make them ill. Example: cholera, amoebiasis, hepatitis spread through water. c) Through sexual contact: Some diseases like AIDS and syphilis, etc., are transmitted by sexual contact. Other than this, AIDS virus also spreads through blood, infected syringes, infected mother to her baby during pregnancy and through breast feeding. d) Through vectors: There are some animals which act as intermediaries or vectors for particular diseases. The vectors carry diseases from infected person to the healthy person. For example, mosquito spreads malaria causing organism in humans, while sucking their blood.
final_answer: Therefore, infectious diseases can spread through air, water, sexual contact, and vectors.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of various transmission methods of diseases.

subject: science
question_text: What precautions can you take in your school to reduce the incidence of infectious diseases?
answer_text: To prevent the incidence of infectious diseases in school, the following precautions can be taken: a) Avoid contact of students suffering from air borne diseases like common cold, cough, eye, flu, etc. b) By checking the availability of clean drinking water in school. c) Clean surroundings in school will not allow the growth and multiplication of vectors. d) Starting childhood immunisation programmes in schools.
final_answer: Thus, implementing these precautions can significantly reduce the spread of infectious diseases in schools.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding and applying health precautions.
